conclusions.rationale: The four semantic dispositions, exact grounding and unsupported-scope rejection are observable; equivalent behavior and justified technical necessities are distinguished from contradictions.

conclusions.rationale: Negated prohibition mentions are explicitly permitted, while Normative Identity v2 narrowly defines lifecycle normalization and all other stale-review causes.

conclusions.rationale: The six-versus-five scenario gives a concrete preservation and blocking oracle, and accepted changes preserve IDs while invalidating affected proof.

conclusions.rationale: The criterion requires passing behavioral assertions, independent runner capture/report provenance, invocation ownership and before/after governed identity; unmapped ACs cannot inherit certification.

conclusions.rationale: Each invalid evidence class has an explicit rejection outcome even when the process exits zero; lifecycle-only changes are separately bounded by Normative Identity v2.

conclusions.rationale: Driver execution remains possible while insufficient proof leaves certification unavailable, so operational use is not confused with acceptance evidence.

conclusions.rationale: Generation outcomes, attempts, duration and runtime/model identity are separately recorded; absent cost and unexecuted runtimes cannot become success claims.

conclusions.rationale: Routine deterministic checks, bounded core-change samples and full release/model/runtime corpora have distinct triggers; unavailable runtimes explicitly prevent parity claims.
